text.en: Asha touched a hot pan and pulled her hand away before she even thought. "That is a reflex," said her teacher.

The nervous system controls and coordinates body activities. Its unit is the neuron, made of the cell body, dendrites and an axon. Neurons are sensory, motor or association neurons, and nerve fibres can be myelinated or non-myelinated. An impulse passes along a neuron as an electrical signal. At most synapses it is relayed by chemicals called neurotransmitters.
The central nervous system consists of the brain and spinal cord. The brain is protected by the skull and bathed in cerebrospinal fluid. A reflex action is a quick automatic response. A spinal reflex arc can organise withdrawal, while some other reflexes are coordinated in the brainstem.
The peripheral nervous system has cranial and spinal nerves, and the autonomic nervous system controls involuntary actions like heartbeat through its sympathetic and parasympathetic parts.

text.en: Light can change and a surface can become hotter. Receptors help turn such changes into signals the nervous system can use.

board.text: A stimulus is a detectable change

text.en: If you notice a dropped ball, your eyes detect movement. Your muscles receive signals that help you reach out.

board.text: A response is what the body does next

text.en: The short branches help a neuron receive signals from other cells. The cell body contains the nucleus and supports the cell.

board.text: Dendrites receive many signals

text.en: The axon carries a signal towards its terminals. Depending on the neuron, the destination may be another neuron or a muscle.

board.text: The axon carries an impulse away

text.en: Myelin wraps around sections of some axons. Gaps between the wrapped parts help impulses travel more quickly along many of those fibres.

board.text: Myelin insulates some axons

text.en: A neuron is one cell. A nerve contains many nerve fibres and supporting tissue.

board.text: A nerve is a bundle of fibres

text.en: When an impulse reaches an axon terminal, chemical messengers cross the gap and bind to the receiving cell.

board.text: Signals cross most synapses chemically

text.en: A sensory neuron carries information from receptors towards the brain or spinal cord. It is part of an incoming path.

board.text: Sensory signals travel into the CNS

text.en: A motor neuron carries instructions towards a muscle or gland. A responding muscle or gland is called an effector.

board.text: Motor signals travel out to effectors

text.en: An interneuron can link a sensory neuron to a motor neuron. Many such connections help the central nervous system combine information.

board.text: Interneurons link paths within the CNS

text.en: For a ball rolling towards you, the cerebrum helps interpret what you see and plan the voluntary movement needed to catch it.

board.text: The cerebrum helps interpret and plan

text.en: The cerebellum helps make actions smoother and supports balance. It contributes when you adjust your position on uneven ground.

board.text: The cerebellum helps coordinate movement

text.en: The medulla is part of the brainstem. It helps regulate breathing and other automatic functions.

board.text: The medulla helps regulate automatic functions

text.en: The skull is a hard outer protection. Membranes surround the central nervous system, and cerebrospinal fluid helps cushion it.

board.text: Skull, coverings and fluid protect the brain

text.en: Signals from the body can travel to the brain through the spinal cord. Other signals travel from the brain towards the body.

board.text: The spinal cord carries signals both ways

text.en: After contact with something painfully hot, a spinal circuit can trigger withdrawal. The response can begin before conscious recognition.

board.text: A quick response can use a short pathway

text.en: A receptor detects the stimulus. A sensory neuron brings the signal to the spinal cord, where it can pass through an interneuron.

board.text: The reflex route starts with a receptor

text.en: The motor neuron carries a signal to the muscle. The muscle contracts and pulls the hand away.

board.text: The motor neuron carries the final instruction

text.en: Signals can still reach the brain for conscious awareness after the spinal circuit has begun the response.

board.text: The brain can learn what happened

text.en: Cranial nerves connect at the brain and spinal nerves connect at the spinal cord. They carry information between the central system and the body.

board.text: Peripheral nerves connect the CNS to the body

text.en: The autonomic nervous system helps regulate heart rate and digestion. These adjustments generally happen without a deliberate decision.

board.text: Autonomic control adjusts internal functions

text.en: When you are startled, sympathetic signalling can increase heart rate. Parasympathetic signalling helps slow it again during rest.

board.text: Sympathetic and parasympathetic responses differ

problem.en: Name the two parts of the central nervous system.

text.en: The central part commands the body.
It is made of the brain.
And the spinal cord.

problem.en: Trace the withdrawal reflex after a finger touches a hot surface.

text.en: A receptor detects the stimulus and a sensory neuron brings the signal to the spinal cord.

why.en: This is the incoming part of the arc.

text.en: An interneuron relays the signal to a motor neuron, and a muscle contracts.

why.en: The motor signal completes the route to the effector.

problem.en: A person steadies their posture on a moving bus. Which brain area helps coordinate that adjustment?

text.en: Choose the cerebellum.

why.en: It contributes to balance and coordinated movement.

text.en: It helps refine muscle actions as body position changes.

why.en: Coordination draws on information from several parts of the nervous system.

problem.en: Why is a resting heartbeat different from choosing to open your hand?

text.en: Heart rate is adjusted by autonomic signalling.

why.en: This usually happens without a deliberate decision.

text.en: Opening a hand deliberately is voluntary movement.

why.en: Motor commands to skeletal muscle can be planned consciously.

requiredIdeas.en: Reflexes are quick, spinal cord responses.
They do not wait for thinking.
